mem.t: Don’t be drunken with wine, in which is dissipation, but be filled with the Spirit,

lessons.title: The Spirit of Pentecost
lessons.theme: The Spirit came down, bringing God's presence to dwell in every believer

v: Now when the day of Pentecost had come, they were all with one accord in one place.
Suddenly there came from the sky a sound like the rushing of a mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.
Tongues like fire appeared and were distributed to them, and one sat on each of them.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak with other languages, as the Spirit gave them the ability to speak.

lessons.still: Breathe quietly, and consider that breath and wind are both invisible, yet real. Say to the Lord, “Holy Spirit, you already live in me.” Don't seek an unusual feeling; ask only to become more aware of his presence.
teach: However beautiful a sailing boat is, without wind it can only sit in the harbour; what the sailor can do is raise the sail and turn it to catch the wind. In the first stage we learned that the Holy Spirit lives in our hearts and that we are to live from the heart by the Spirit. This week we go a step further: being filled with the Spirit. We begin back at the starting point — Pentecost.

Pentecost was originally a harvest festival, when the firstfruits of the wheat were offered. When God came down on Mount Sinai there was thunder and fire; now the Spirit comes like a mighty wind and tongues of fire. The law was carved on tablets of stone, but the Spirit writes God's word on human hearts (Jeremiah 31:33; 2 Corinthians 3:3). The text says, “They were all filled with the Holy Spirit” — all of them, not a few spiritual elites.

The coming of the Spirit at Pentecost was a once-for-all event in the history of redemption, like the cross and the resurrection; yet in Acts, “being filled with the Spirit” happens again and again (Acts 4:8, 4:31). Here is the change of mindset: the Holy Spirit is not a force for us to use but a Person, God himself, who wants to direct us. The question is not “How much of the Spirit do I have?” but “How much of me does the Spirit have?”
lessons.light: 321 Light: Among the three foundations is this: the Holy Spirit is my guide. Being filled is not chasing a feeling but yielding control — only the self-emptied life can be led by the Spirit. The path of service begins with “Spirit”: first the Spirit's guidance, then understanding of the truth, the life of Jesus, and true ministry.
q: Who is God? — The Spirit came like wind and fire. What does that show you about God's presence?
Who am I? — Do you tend to treat the Holy Spirit as a power, or as the Lord who wants to direct you?
How shall I respond? — In what matter today will you “raise your sail” and wait for the Spirit's guidance?
lessons.jesus: After Jesus was baptised, the Holy Spirit descended on him like a dove (Luke 3:22); “full of the Holy Spirit, he returned from the Jordan” (Luke 4:1) and began his ministry. If even the Son of God relied on the Spirit in his ministry on earth, how much more must we?
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, thank you for coming down at Pentecost and for living in me. I don't ask for an extraordinary experience; I ask only that you would have more of me. I raise the sail of my life — blow on me and guide me, and govern my thoughts, words and actions today. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Read Acts 2 and circle every mention of the Holy Spirit
Before making a decision, pause for three seconds and silently ask, “Holy Spirit, what do you want?”
Thank God for a past time when you experienced the Spirit's guidance
lessons.noon: “They were all filled with the Holy Spirit.” — Lord, right now I open myself to your Spirit.

lessons.title: Signs of Being Filled
lessons.theme: The evidence of being filled with the Spirit is praise, thanksgiving and mutual submission

v: Don’t be drunken with wine, in which is dissipation, but be filled with the Spirit,
speaking to one another in psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs; singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord;
giving thanks always concerning all things in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to God, even the Father;
subjecting yourselves to one another in the fear of Christ.

lessons.still: Hum a hymn or worship song you know well, aloud or in your heart. Let the words become a prayer. Then be still, and count three things you can give thanks for right now, naming them slowly one by one.
teach: When someone is drunk, everyone around can tell: their speech, their walk and their face are all under the control of alcohol. Paul contrasts being “drunken with wine” with being “filled with the Spirit.” In both cases a power takes control, but the results are opposite: wine leads to dissipation, while the Spirit makes us more and more like Christ.

After “be filled” in verse 18, the original text continues with several participles describing the life that naturally flows from a filled person: speaking to one another in psalms and hymns (building one another up in relationship), singing and making melody to the Lord (worship toward God), giving thanks to the Father for all things (our attitude toward circumstances), and submitting to one another in the fear of Christ (humility with others). Immediately after this, Paul turns to the relationships of husbands and wives, parents and children, masters and servants.

Many assume the sign of being filled with the Spirit must be some dramatic experience, but what Paul mentions first here is praise on our lips, thanksgiving in our hearts and submission in our relationships. Here is the change of mindset: the evidence of being filled shows up not only in church meetings, but even more at home, at work, and in how others experience us.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The first sign of a Spirit-filled person is that Jesus is glorified; the last is mutual submission — humility draws out humility, and relationships become a win for both sides. Giving thanks in everything is the “God” step of the path of service: all glory to God. God's kingdom system is built in homes and churches like these.
q: Who is God? — The Spirit makes melody in our hearts. How does he long for us to relate to God?
Who am I? — What do others see in you more — being “filled with emotions” or being “filled with the Spirit”?
How shall I respond? — In which relationship today will you practise “subjecting yourselves to one another”?
lessons.jesus: Jesus “rejoiced in the Holy Spirit” and gave thanks to the Father (Luke 10:21); he submitted to the Father and gladly served people. His whole life was one of praise, thanksgiving and submission — the most beautiful picture of a Spirit-filled life.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, fill me and govern me. May there be praise on my lips and thanksgiving in my heart, and may I submit to others in the fear of Christ, at home and at work. Do not let emotions or desires control me; let you control me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Sing or quietly recite at least one song of praise today
Before bed, write down five things you are thankful for, including one difficulty
At home or at work, choose once to defer to someone rather than push to be first
lessons.noon: “But be filled with the Spirit” — Lord, right now govern my heart and my lips.

lessons.title: Being Filled Is Ongoing Obedience
lessons.theme: Being filled is not a one-time experience but following him step by step

v: Those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh with its passions and lusts.
If we live by the Spirit, let’s also walk by the Spirit.
Don’t grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.

lessons.still: Think back over today so far. Was there a moment of unease, as if you brushed past a gentle prompting? Quietly tell the Lord, “Holy Spirit, I'm sorry. I'm willing to obey right now.”
teach: Hold a cup under a tap upside down, and no matter how much water flows, none will go in. The key to being filled is not a shortage of water but the posture of the cup. In the original, “be filled” in Ephesians 5:18 is a present, passive command: keep on letting the Spirit fill you.

Galatians says that those who belong to Christ have “crucified the flesh with its passions and lusts”; since we “live by the Spirit,” we should also “walk by the Spirit.” The word for “walk” here carries the idea of falling into line and advancing step by step — keeping in step with the Spirit. Ephesians reminds us not to grieve the Spirit: he is a Person who can be grieved, not cold, impersonal energy.

What grieves the Spirit? The surrounding verses list lying, letting the sun go down on our anger, stealing, corrupt speech, bitterness and wrath (Ephesians 4:25–31). So last week's confession and forgiveness were exactly the preparation for being filled. Here is the change of mindset: we are filled not by chasing more but by obeying more — every act of obedience makes room for the Spirit.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Living from the heart by the Spirit means obeying his promptings in small things; living from the head by yourself means hearing him but stopping to calculate first. Self-rule leads the march itself; self-emptying keeps in step behind the Spirit. Obedience is not losing freedom but entering the limitless.
q: Who is God? — The Spirit can be “grieved.” What does that reveal about God's heart?
Who am I? — Is there a recent prompting of the Spirit that you have still not obeyed?
How shall I respond? — What step of obedience will you take today to keep in step with the Spirit?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he sees the Father doing” (John 5:19). Every step of his life was in step with the Father. He did not obey occasionally but continually — and that is the Spirit-filled life.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, I confess that I often grieve you, hearing your promptings and not obeying. Please forgive me. Today I want to follow you step by step and obey your promptings in small things. Keep on filling me and govern every part of my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Obey right away a prompting of the Spirit you have long put off
Today, notice a bitter word you're about to say, and choose not to say it
In the evening, review: which steps today kept in step with the Spirit, and where did I fall behind?
lessons.noon: “If we live by the Spirit, let’s also walk by the Spirit.” — Lord, right now I keep in step with you.

lessons.title: Power for Witness
lessons.theme: The Spirit's power is not for ourselves but for bearing witness to Christ

v: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth.”
When they had prayed, the place was shaken where they were gathered together. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with boldness.

lessons.still: Quietly bring to mind a relative or friend who does not yet know the Lord, and bring their name before him. Say to the Lord, “Lord, I am timid, but your Spirit is powerful. Please give me an opportunity, and give me courage.”
teach: Connect electricity to a light bulb and it shines; connect it to a motor and the machine turns — power always has a purpose. Before he ascended, Jesus promised his disciples, “You will receive power,” and immediately explained why: “You will be witnesses to me.” The Spirit's power is not for showing off our spiritual experiences but for letting Christ be seen.

Acts 1:8 sketches an ever-widening circle: from Jerusalem to Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth — which is also the outline of the whole book of Acts. In chapter 4, when Peter and John were threatened and ordered never again to speak in the name of Jesus, the church's response was not to ask for their enemies to disappear but to pray; and “they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with boldness.” One of the fruits of being filled is boldness.

This same Peter had once denied the Lord in front of a servant girl; filled with the Spirit, he boldly bore witness before the Council. His change came not from willpower but from the Holy Spirit. Here is the change of mindset: witnessing is not selling religion but telling what Jesus has done for me; my weakness is the very place where the Spirit's power is displayed.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The Spirit's witness is focused on Jesus, not on the witness — this is letting Jesus receive all the glory. Of the five changes, “ministry” is built on “life” and “relationships”: first be filled, then bear witness; first live out Christ, then speak of Christ.
q: Who is God? — God promised power to timid disciples. What is his heart toward your weakness?
Who am I? — Who is in your “Jerusalem” — the harvest field nearest to you?
How shall I respond? — For whom will you ask today for an opportunity and the courage to bear witness?
lessons.jesus: In the synagogue at Nazareth Jesus read, “The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to preach good news to the poor” (Luke 4:18). His power was always used to set people free, heal them and bring them back to the Father.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that I am often timid about bearing witness to you. Fill me with your Holy Spirit and give me courage and wisdom — not to show off myself, but so that people may see you. Give me an opportunity today to tell someone near me what you have done in my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down three people in your “Jerusalem” who don't yet believe
Pray for one of them, asking for a natural opportunity to share
Write “What Jesus has done for me” in three sentences
lessons.noon: “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you.” — Lord, right now make me bold to bear witness to you.

lessons.title: Asking to Be Filled Every Day
lessons.theme: Like drinking water when we are thirsty, we come to the Lord daily to receive the Spirit

v: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?”
Now on the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried out, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink!
He who believes in me, as the Scripture has said, from within him will flow rivers of living water.”

lessons.still: Feel your own thirst: weariness, emptiness, being stretched beyond your strength. Don't hide it; tell the Lord plainly, “Lord, I am thirsty.” Then, as if taking a drink of water, quietly receive: “I believe you are filling me right now.”
teach: No one can quench today's thirst with water drunk last week, and a phone can't last today on a charge from last month. Spiritual life is the same. Ephesians 5:18 is a continuous command, so being filled is not a certificate on file but something we receive every day.

On the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus cried out, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink!” John goes on to explain that he was speaking of the Spirit whom those who believed in him would receive (7:39). The contrast in Luke 11:13 is simple: if even imperfect fathers give their children good things, “how much more” your heavenly Father? When we ask for the Spirit, we are not beggars pleading for scraps but children asking their Father.

This week we have seen that the Spirit of Pentecost has come; that the signs of being filled are praise, thanksgiving and submission; that being filled is ongoing obedience; and that power is for witness. Today we put it into a simple daily habit: each morning, admit your thirst, confess and be emptied, hand over control, and receive by faith. Next week we face a closely related subject: the root of pride and its remedy.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Asking to be filled every day is admitting that “apart from the Lord I can do nothing” — the prayer of the self-emptied life. Living from the head by yourself leaves you drier and drier; living from the heart by the Spirit lets living water well up. The rivers flowing out of us are meant to water our “2” and bear the ninefold fruit of the Spirit — this is 920.
q: Who is God? — “How much more your heavenly Father” — do you believe God is glad to give you the Holy Spirit?
Who am I? — How high is your spiritual “water level” right now? What is making you thirsty?
How shall I respond? — At what moment each day will you build the habit of asking to be filled?
lessons.jesus: Jesus often withdrew to the wilderness to pray (Luke 5:16). Even the Son of God needed daily fellowship with the Father, receiving from him. At the well he told the Samaritan woman that the water he gives becomes a spring within (John 4:14) — and that spring wells up toward us today.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, I confess that I am thirsty; on my own I have run dry. I come before you, confess my sins, hand over my control, and by faith receive the Holy Spirit you have promised. Fill me today, and let living water flow out from me to refresh the people around me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Tomorrow morning, make your first act a one-sentence prayer to be filled with the Spirit
Write “Admit thirst, confess, hand over, receive” on a sticky note
lessons.noon: “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink!” — Lord, right now I come to drink your living water.
